claims.summary: For a commutative ring A and F=(F_1,...,F_r), r>=1, with F dot c=1, every syzygy h is sum_(i<j)(h_i c_j-h_j c_i)(F_j e_i-F_i e_j). Thus the pairwise Koszul vectors generate ker F. In A[Y], the ideals I=(Y_i) and J=(Y_i-F_i) are comaximal, so the general IPS zero-certificate ideal I intersect J equals IJ, generated by Y_i(Y_j-F_j). Over a polynomial ring over a field these generators have degree bounded by the input degrees (or max(2,1+max deg F_i) for the ideal generators) and polynomial-size presentations from the input circuits. The displayed filling coefficients use the supplied certificate c; no degree or circuit bound independent of c is inferred.
claims.assessment: Working standard unit-row Koszul and comaximal-ideal calculations passed by the sole fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer. Explicit generators are distinguished from efficient filling coefficients; no literature novelty or lower-bound gain. The parent size-sensitive invariant task remains open.
claims.rationale: Tests the concrete finite-generation step of the queued certificate-coset recipe rather than assuming that a nice generator list supplies a complexity invariant.
claims.next_action: Construct a specific size-sensitive property stable under all generator multiples; the explicit generator list does not discharge that retained task.

claims.summary: For any polynomial tuple F over any field, adjoin F_0=0 and pair generators K_ij=F_j e_i-F_i e_j for 0<=i<j<=r. Hilbert-like certificates C(x,Y) for F are equivalent in arithmetic circuit size, depth and old coefficient-degree ceilings to Hilbert-like coefficient encodings H(x,Z)=sum a_ij(x)Z_ij whose vector specialization sum a_ij K_ij equals the constant vector e_0. Forward conversion renames Y_j to Z_0j. Reverse conversion sets Z_0j=Y_j and every Z_ij with i>0 to zero. Neither operation increases size or depth; the statement includes simultaneous nonexistence. This is a calibration of filling complexity with explicit small generators, not a new hard formula or an assertion that every unpadded target filling is hard.
claims.assessment: Working exact placeholder-substitution equivalence passed by the sole fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer, retaining all original generators including Boolean axioms. The zero equation changes no satisfiability condition and supplies no lower bound.
claims.rationale: Shows that the missing circuit cost can reside in filling even a constant syzygy with the explicit pair generators; finite generation alone leaves the original certificate problem.
claims.next_action: Preserve the full-certificate alternative and its queued size-sensitive task; a new extractor must address filling complexity rather than finite generation.
